title: Bees in the City
text:
Last month, a famous magazine published an article about city bees. The writer visited a rooftop garden in London where beekeepers keep hives. She said the bees there make honey with a sweet taste, because the flowers come from many gardens.

The article also explained why bees are important. Bees help plants grow by moving pollen from one flower to another. Without them, many fruits and vegetables would be harder to find in shops. Many readers wrote letters to say they now plant flowers on their balconies.

options: A shop in the city centre

questions.text: What do bees do to help plants grow?
options: They move pollen from one flower to another
They build hives in tall trees

questions.text: Why did many readers start planting flowers on their balconies?
options: The article inspired them to help bees
They wanted to sell flowers in shops
They had to move to a new house
Their school asked them to do it

questions.text: What can the reader infer about the honey from the rooftop hives?
options: It may taste different because the bees visit many gardens
It is always sold in plastic bottles
It comes from a farm outside London
It is not sweet at all

vocabulary.definition: people who look after bees and their hives
boxes or homes where bees live and make honey
a fine yellow powder from flowers that helps plants make seeds

paragraph_translations: El mes pasado, una famosa revista publicó un artículo sobre las abejas de la ciudad. La escritora visitó un jardín en la azotea de Londres donde los apicultores tienen colmenas. Ella dijo que las abejas de allí hacen miel de sabor dulce, porque las flores vienen de muchos jardines.

El artículo también explicó por qué las abejas son importantes. Las abejas ayudan a las plantas a crecer al trasladar el polen de una flor a otra. Sin ellas, muchas frutas y verduras serían más difíciles de encontrar en las tiendas. Muchos lectores escribieron cartas para decir que ahora plantan flores en sus balcones.
